A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAE-based investigation of SDXL Turbo. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the extensive reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original feature interventions, interpretability and sensitivity measurements, block ablations, reconstruction experiments, and spatial-position probe accuracies.

after.justification: V2 retains original quantitative and qualitative experiments and adds four-step SDXL Turbo interventions and exploratory PixArt-LCM XL results.

M1.justification: The per-block TopK SAEs, auxiliary loss, residual-update inputs, activation modulation, and empty-prompt interventions remain unchanged. Freely specified spatial masks were already demonstrated in v1 Appendix D and Figure 10. Applying SAEs to PixArt does not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The documented coverage remains text-to-image generation and feature intervention using LAION-COCO prompts, with real-world texture images as a reference. Four-step generation and PixArt extend model and inference settings; no distinct additional dataset, domain, or task is documented.

E2.justification: Random, Same Prompt, and Textures remain the comparators in v1 Table 1(a) and v2 Table 1. The annotation-based random comparisons and unmodified-generation controls are also retained. No competing interpretability method is added.

E3.justification: V2 adds exploratory protocols: Appendix D applies identical intervention maps and strengths across four denoising steps, while Appendix H studies PixArt blocks 6, 9, and 25 during four-step generation. The retained SDXL experiments keep their training settings, metrics, and intervention strengths.

E4.justification: Appendices D and H substantially broaden the applicability questions investigated through one-step-to-four-step transfer and feature localization and causal behavior in another architecture. V1's spatial-position linear-probe check is removed. Existing block ablations, reconstruction and sparsity analyses, and random-feature galleries are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations. V2 Section 5.2 additionally distinguishes feature-score variability from uncertainty in the mean, gives an approximate interval M ± 0.055S using 1,280 elements, and asserts widespread statistical significance. This adds uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: All matched quantitative tables, feature captions, and prompt tables retain their values. V2 adds editing examples, qualitative preservation of feature effects in four-step SDXL generation, and PixArt activation findings with typically weak individual causal effects. It removes the spatial-probe accuracies of 97.9%, 98.48%, 99.44%, and 95.57% reported in v1.

T1.justification: V2 removes the formal diffusion account in v1 Section 2.2 and Appendix G, including the Gaussian corruption definition, KL/noise-prediction reasoning, and adversarial-distillation objective. SAE and superposition mathematics largely remain. V2 Appendix E Equation 12 also omits the activation operator present in v1 Equation 13, inconsistently with its surrounding explanation.

C1.justification: The abstract's central claims about interpretable, causal SAE features and block specialization remain unchanged. V2's conclusion adds an explicit claim that features learned during one-step generation can modify two-to-four-step generation, extending the stated applicability beyond v1's empirical focus.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands discussion of applicability to larger architectures and multiple denoising steps, interprets four-step transfer, and suggests PixArt causal effects may require feature combinations. It removes v1's explicit discussion of overlapping block roles and its broader concern that short VLM captions inadequately describe complex, context-dependent features.

D1.justification: Core SAE hyperparameters, annotation templates, and code/demo access remain. V2 newly discloses the 1,280-element sample underlying its uncertainty estimate and provides limited settings for the added experiments. It removes the separate supplementary-material link and the pointer to first-100-feature visualization galleries.

R1.justification: Section 6 replaces the image-editing survey with positioning against layer/timestep-specialization studies by Agarwal, Voynov, and Zhang's ProSpect, explaining differences in supervision and where specialization occurs. V2 also adds PixArt and crosscoder references while removing numerous editing and diffusion-background citations. The central SAE-related comparisons remain.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the diffusion background, related work, and discussion, and adds an accessible introduction to the visualization techniques. The random-feature case study moves from Section 4.3 into Appendix C, appendices are reorganized, and the extended diffusion-background appendix is removed.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document to two columns, splits v1 Table 1 into Tables 1 and 2, and extensively resizes and relocates retained displays. It adds editing, four-step, and PixArt galleries and a main-text copy of the U-net diagram. The original qualitative image content is retained.

improvement.justification: The four-step transfer evidence and candid PixArt causal limitations in Appendices D and H modestly improve the assessment of applicability. Clearer visualization explanations, uncertainty reporting, and research positioning also help. These gains outweigh the limited losses from removed qualifications and the introduced encoder-equation inconsistency, but the added experiments remain exploratory and the central quantitative evidence is unchanged.
